ai_insight.geomorphic_summary: The multi-pass fusion reveals a complex south-polar impact structure (~21 km diameter) exhibiting sharp, un-eroded rim crests and pronounced hummocky ejecta blankets. The central uplift peak is distinctly resolved with steep (~28°) slopes and structural fracturing, while inner wall terraces show clear slump blocks preserved without motion blurring.
ai_insight.illumination_assessment: Combining four distinct solar azimuth angles (45°, 135°, 225°, and 315°) eliminated 78% of uninformative saturation and deep shadows present in single-pass imagery. Low-elevation passes (20°-22°) accentuated micro-topography along the western and eastern rims, while the high-sun pass (52°) preserved albedo optical maturity and radial ejecta filament contrast.
ai_insight.permanently_shadowed_regions: The crater floor exhibits an extensive Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR) where direct solar incidence has remained 0.0° for >2 Gyr. Secondary scattered light modeling in the fused mosaic reveals subtle interior floor roughness, indicating low thermal conductivity regolith and prospective surface volatile/water-ice trapping zones.
ai_insight.reconstruction_confidence_notes: Homography alignment achieved a mean reprojection error of 1.15 pixels, well within sub-pixel photogrammetric tolerances. Distance-feathered multi-band blending prevented tile seam artifacts, yielding a continuous photometric surface suitable for high-precision digital elevation modeling.
recommendations: Design robotic egress routes along the northwestern rim terrace where Observation B provides optimal 0.5m boulder hazard detection.
Deploy active optical or flash-LIDAR illumination when penetrating the 3.8 km interior PSR boundary line.
Conduct multi-spectral reflectance calibration across the bright radial rays highlighted by Observation D to assess space weathering maturity.
